custody.headSubject: D-118: record offline-analysis-closure-contract.v3 as DR-106 successor candidate
custody.motionScope: The appended D-119 and D-118 decisions record successor candidates for DR-113 and DR-106 respectively and do not alter D-012, DR-104, file 08, or this subject.

measurements.detail: The prompt and subject reproduce their dispatched digests. The subject is strict duplicate-key-free JSON at mode 0444 and remained byte-identical.

The D-117 COORD image is an exact 257447-byte prefix of the final D-118 HEAD, with a 6224-byte append that records unrelated DR-113 replay-purge and DR-106 offline-analysis candidates. File 08 and the subject are unmoved, satisfying the prompt's explicit exception.
File 02 lines 76-79 and COORD lines 1065-1119 match the carried arrays exactly. The live DR-104 row is unique and byte-exact.

The artifact uses the exact file 08 token DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED. No status or standing field regresses DR-104 to leftover-design or OPEN; the only such phrase is review guidance identifying that regression as a finding.

The explicit deferrals preserve namespace depth beyond mounted roots and third-party transfer/dispute on the DR-117 successor/DR-010 path. The candidate binds NOTHING, leaves negative tests unauthored/unexecuted, claims no row satisfaction, mints no D-096 (A) grant, and authorizes no implementation.

The extraction ends at COORD line 1119 and omits D-012's adopted C-D012 integration properties at lines 1129-1136. The subject contains no per-install uniqueness scope, no provenance-bound (ID, provenance) discriminator, and no host-core release-train definition for the alias window. It also omits the decided-policy bounding preamble at lines 1061-1064, including the explicit deny-by-default bound.

D-012 item 3 makes reserved-list/live-grammar CI parity part of negative-test evidence. The subject preserves that sentence in the carry and decidedClauses.hostReserved, but omits the parity class from negativeTestClasses.classes.

attacks.claimAttacked: The candidate integrates the adopted D-012 identity and alias policy rather than only its numbered core.
attacks.method: Read the D-012 adoption context before and after numbered items 1-7, then search every subject string for the routed integration constraints.
evidence: COORD lines 1129-1136 say the registry uniqueness universe is PER-INSTALL, custody records are provenance-bound with (ID, provenance) as the same-versus-different-component discriminator, and one minor release cycle means the HOST CORE release train.
None of PER-INSTALL, provenance, (ID, provenance), HOST CORE, or release train appears anywhere in the subject.

The omission is operationally material: the carried item-1 phrase global uniqueness is left without its adopted per-install scope, custody collision behavior is underdefined, and alias retention can be timed against the wrong release train.

attacks.claimAttacked: The named negative-test classes cover all tests D-012 explicitly assigns to negative evidence.
attacks.method: Compare D-012 items 3 and 7 with negativeTestClasses.classes rather than treating the clause-7 list as the whole evidence roster.
evidence: The ten clause-7 classes are reproduced exactly.
The separate item-3 CI parity test is named only in prose and is absent from the machine-readable classes array used to route qualification evidence.

attacks.claimAttacked: The artifact regresses file 08 to leftover-design/OPEN or silently takes back deferred namespace and transfer policy.
attacks.method: Resolve DR-104 by row ID, inspect every status/standing field, and compare explicitlyDeferred and identityDependencies with D-012 item 6.
evidence: The exact token is DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED and the row remains unsatisfied without being mislabeled OPEN.
Namespace depth beyond mounted roots and third-party transfer/dispute remain explicitly deferred to DR-117 successor/DR-010.

attacks.claimAttacked: The candidate invents deeper namespace policy, executes tests, advances readiness, mints a grant, or authorizes implementation.
attacks.method: Inspect authorityClaim, status/binds, explicitlyDeferred, negativeTestClasses, whatThisDoesNotDo, and the live row.
evidence: All such authority remains expressly denied and the test classes remain NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED.
The findings require a corrected successor candidate, not application or row satisfaction.

blockers.title: The D-012 extraction omits adopted integration constraints that determine identity scope, custody discrimination, and alias timing.
blockers.finding: d012DecidedPolicyCarriedVerbatim stops at numbered item 7 on COORD line 1119. D-012's adopted file-08/C-D012 integration paragraph immediately afterward records four routed properties, three of which are product semantics: uniqueness is PER-INSTALL rather than unbounded global, the two custody records are provenance-bound and use (ID, provenance) to distinguish the same component from a different one, and the one-minor-release-cycle alias floor is measured on the HOST CORE release train. The subject carries none of those terms. Its source slice also begins after D-012's manifest-first, deny-by-default bounding sentence. A purported leftover integration contract can therefore direct a conforming reader to the wrong uniqueness universe, an incomplete custody rule, and an ambiguous alias clock while claiming to extract D-012's decided policy.
blockers.requiredRepair: Publish a successor that carries the complete adopted policy boundary and C-D012 integration properties from the pinned source; map at least per-install uniqueness, provenance-bound (ID, provenance) discrimination, the host-core release-train alias definition, and deny-by-default into decidedClauses and the applicable negative-test routing. Preserve the report-ahead/per-item landing property as provenance discipline. Keep the file 08 token DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, keep deferred scope deferred, and claim no DR-104 satisfaction or D-096 (A) grant.

shouldFix.title: The negative-test class roster omits D-012's reserved-list/live-grammar parity test.
shouldFix.finding: D-012 item 3 explicitly makes a CI parity test between the static reserved root-command list and live grammar part of negative-test evidence. The subject preserves that requirement in d012DecidedPolicyCarriedVerbatim and decidedClauses.hostReserved, but negativeTestClasses.classes lists only the ten item-7 classes. A qualification consumer following the structured class roster can therefore omit a decided test.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add a reserved-list/live-grammar CI parity entry to negativeTestClasses.classes, or make the structured roster explicitly exhaustive across both D-012 items 3 and 7. Keep execution at qualification and do not claim fixtures are authored.

verdictRule: ACCEPT only when blockers=0 and shouldFix=0.
coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX. The artifact correctly preserves DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, all deferrals, and zero authority/readiness effect, and the D-119/D-118 append-only motion is PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT. But it omits D-012's adopted per-install, provenance-bound custody, host-core release-train, and deny-by-default integration constraints, and its structured negative-test roster drops the reserved-list/live-grammar parity class. DR-104 remains unsatisfied.
